name: Elbit Systems Limited

header.one_liner: Israeli listed defence OEM (NASDAQ/TASE: ESLT) with a genuine India military-aerospace footprint: the Adani-Elbit UAV complex at Hyderabad (Hermes 900 / Drishti 10 Starliner, first India-made UAV delivered to the Navy Jan 2024) and the Elbit DASH helmet-mounted display fitted to the HAL Tejas.

what_it_is.prose: Elbit Systems Limited (NASDAQ/TASE: ESLT) is an Israeli listed defence-electronics and UAV OEM headquartered in Haifa. Its India military-aerospace footprint has two main strands. First, the Adani-Elbit joint venture operates the Adani Elbit UAV Complex in Hyderabad (~50,000 sq ft, inaugurated 2018-19) — the first private UAV manufacturing facility in India and the first Hermes 900 production line outside Israel; the Indian Navy received its first India-made UAV, the Drishti 10 Starliner (Indian designation for the Hermes 900 StarLiner), from this facility in January 2024, and the site has also exported Hermes 900 airframes to Israel. Second, Elbit supplies aircraft mission electronics used on Indian platforms — most visibly the DASH (Display and Sight Helmet) helmet-mounted display fitted to the HAL Tejas, with an upgrade to the DASH-V generation reported for the Tejas Mk1A. Elbit was awarded a $120 million international Hermes 900 contract in September 2025. The Indian Navy has, however, experienced two Hermes 900 (Drishti 10) crashes within 18 months — the first in January 2025 and the second in July 2026 — raising reliability questions that the Navy is investigating.

deployments_procurement.summary: Elbit's India military-aerospace footprint is anchored by the Adani-Elbit UAV complex at Hyderabad, which delivered the Indian Navy's first India-made UAV (Drishti 10 Starliner / Hermes 900) in January 2024 and exports Hermes 900 airframes to Israel. Elbit's DASH helmet-mounted display equips the HAL Tejas, with a DASH-V upgrade reported for the Mk1A. Two Indian Navy Hermes 900 crashes have occurred within 18 months.

faq.question: What is the Adani-Elbit joint venture and what does it build?
faq.answer: The Adani-Elbit joint venture operates the Adani Elbit UAV Complex in Hyderabad (~50,000 sq ft, inaugurated 2018-19) — the first private UAV manufacturing facility in India and the first Hermes 900 production line outside Israel. It builds the Hermes 900 (designated Drishti 10 Starliner in Indian service) and delivered the Indian Navy its first India-made UAV in January 2024, while also exporting Hermes 900 airframes to Israel.

faq.question: Does Elbit supply the helmet-mounted display for the HAL Tejas?
faq.answer: Yes. The Elbit DASH (Display and Sight Helmet) helmet-mounted display is fitted to the HAL Tejas, giving the pilot symbology and off-boresight targeting cueing. An upgrade to the DASH-V generation has been reported for the Tejas Mk1A, phasing out the earlier DASH-IV.

faq.question: What are the Hermes 900 reliability concerns in Indian Navy service?
faq.answer: Two Indian Navy Hermes 900 (Drishti 10 Starliner) UAVs crashed within 18 months — the first in January 2025 and the second in July 2026. The Indian Navy is investigating. Despite the incidents, the Adani-Elbit line continues Hermes 900 production and Elbit won a $120 million international Hermes 900 contract in September 2025.
